hero.headline: Two St. Lucie County cyclospora cases confirmed amid produce outbreak
hero.teaser: Two cases of cyclospora have been confirmed in St. Lucie County since May as part of a wider outbreak linked to contaminated lettuce across the country.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Health has confirmed five local cases of cyclospora since May, including two in St. Lucie County, two in Palm Beach County and one in Martin County. The outbreak centers around lettuce linked to E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the United States have been affected. As reports of contaminated produce spread, many South Florida residents are changing their eating habits and avoiding certain foods altogether.

Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers like bananas, melons and avocados. However, she cautioned that these items still need to be washed before cutting or peeling. She also warned that the outbreak is not an excuse to abandon healthy eating entirely. "It's not an excuse to say to heck with fruits and vegetables and hit the donuts, we want to still remain healthy," Barone said. She noted that beans and nuts are safe alternatives that provide fiber and protein.

Barone recommends avoiding bagged lettuce if possible and instead buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers. Berries, especially raspberries, should be avoided because they are difficult to clean properly. She recommends cleaning produce using a one to three part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce before eating. She also recommends cooking vegetables when possible.

Local residents are taking various precautions in response to the outbreak. Jenny Rhodes, visiting Delray Beach with her daughters Dakota and Brynlee, said her family is staying away from lettuce. "I miss my salads, I miss my berries, better be careful than ruin your day," she said. George Lorenz in West Palm Beach said he is also being cautious. "I've heard that it's going around and I'm trying to stay away from it," Lorenz said. Hendriette Peckens in Boynton Beach reported buying oranges, apples and bread instead of greens and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner. The contaminated produce can cause severe stomach illness and intense diarrhea, prompting many families to steer clear of leafy greens altogether while the outbreak continues.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon as severe storms batter Treasure Coast
cards.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather swept across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to WPTV showed the waterspout moving through the area during the storm system.

Port St. Lucie saw over 3 inches of rain according to weather spotters. Merry Moore O'Rourke, a Port St. Lucie resident, described the conditions: "All of a sudden, it got black. The wind started just raging and the sky had lit up like I have not seen." The storms stretched into Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning.

Port St. Lucie also experienced significant lightning activity. Lucie County Fire District contained a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane after reports that a lightning strike ignited vegetation in a nearby lot. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening storm. Radar picked up a significant amount of lightning in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate the cause and could not confirm what started the blaze.

Moore O'Rourke summed up the experience shared by many across the region: "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary." The severe weather included waterspouts, lightning strikes and fires across the Treasure Coast Friday, demonstrating the unpredictable power of nature.

cards.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian as severe storms batter Treasure Coast
cards.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather left a trail of damage across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area during Friday's storm system.

The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain, dangerous lightning and fires. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotter Merry Moore O'Rourke recorded over 3 inches of rain in her rain gauge. She described the sudden intensity of the storm, saying the sky got black, wind started raging and the sky lit up like she had not seen before. The severe weather extended to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning.

Lightning strikes ignited a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane in Port St. Lucie after vegetation in a nearby lot caught fire. Lucie County Fire District crews contained that blaze. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening storm. Radar picked up significant lightning activity in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Moore O'Rourke summed up the experience many residents felt as the storms moved through the region. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power, from waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires across the affected areas.

cards.headline: JetBlue cancels Vero Beach to New York JFK route in September
cards.body:
JetBlue is canceling its flight route between Vero Beach Regional Airport and New York's JFK Airport, with the last flights operating on Sept. 9. The airline cited low demand as the reason for ending the route, which launched last December to excitement from Treasure Coast residents hoping for convenient travel options to the Northeast.

Brandon Dambeck, interim airport director, said JetBlue was not seeing the ridership numbers it had hoped for on the JFK route. "Just wasn't seeing what they were hoping for," Dambeck said. He added that the decision reflects how the airline industry operates. "It's just the way that that market works, and air carriers will fluctuate based off of demand," Dambeck said. The Boston route from Vero Beach Regional Airport is performing well, according to Dambeck. "Boston is seeing great demand," Dambeck said.

Not everyone agrees the route had a fair shot. Charlie Ahern, who regularly uses JetBlue flights at Vero Beach Regional Airport, said he believes the route would have grown over time. "I think if they hung in there, it would have worked. I think it would have built up pretty good," Ahern said. He said the convenience of flying out of Vero Beach is hard to beat. "It's easy. It's close," Ahern said. Grece Ezzi flew into Vero Beach on JetBlue from Boston on Friday for the first time.

As for whether the JFK route could return in the future, Dambeck said the door is not closed. "They'll evaluate continuously. So just because it's gone now doesn't mean that it never will come back," Dambeck said. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. JetBlue has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

cards.headline: Leon County jury orders Rep. Fabian Basabe to pay $450,000 in harassment case
cards.teaser: A jury found the Republican state representative liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation in a case brought by two former staff members and a mother.
cards.body:
Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation. The case was brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother.

Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training. The trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders. Circuit Judge J. Lee Marsh told him that if an attorney had done half of what he had done, they would have been sanctioned. Basabe told jurors he represented himself because he wanted to demonstrate that he had nothing to hide. After the verdict, however, he acknowledged that proceeding without an attorney was a mistake. Basabe continues to deny the underlying allegations. He has not been criminally charged, and an outside ethics investigation conducted for the Florida House previously reached an inconclusive finding. His political opponents quickly called for his resignation. Basabe is seeking reelection this fall, and the verdict could also renew questions about whether House leaders will pursue disciplinary action.

She warns against bagged lettuce if possible and instead recommends buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers. Barone said consumers should avoid berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. She recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soaking, massaging and cleaning off produce and making sure to cook vegetables.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Edge Palm Beach 3-2 in Extra Innings
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets opened the second half of the season with a 3-2 extra-inning win over the Palm Beach Cardinals on Friday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie scored
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets opened the second half of the season with a 3-2 extra-inning win over the Palm Beach Cardinals on Friday night at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

St. Lucie scored the deciding run in the top of the 10th before Miguel Mejias retired the Cardinals in order to close it out, giving the Mets a 1-0 lead in the three-game series.

Palm Beach struck first on a Sebastian Dos Santos solo home run in the bottom of the first. The early deficit was a tall order for St. Lucie, which came in 16-34 on the season when allowing the first run.

Randy Guzman answered in a hurry in his first game back from the injured list, where he had been since June 9. In his first at-bat, Guzman launched a 108 mph solo homer 374 feet to left to tie it at 1-1 in the second. It was his 10th home run of the season.

Palm Beach edged back ahead in the bottom of the second on a fielder's choice, but St. Lucie answered again when Elian Pena hit his fourth home run of the year to level the score at 2-2.

From there it became a pitchers' duel. Mets starter Joel Lara allowed two runs on four hits over 4 2/3 innings, walking three and striking out five. Zack Mack followed with 1 1/3 scoreless innings and two strikeouts, and Elwis Mijares handled the next three innings, allowing just two hits with no walks and three strikeouts. Mijares earned the win to improve to 4-4.

With the score still tied in the 10th, the Mets started the inning with automatic runner AJ Salgado at second. Branny De Oleo moved him to third with a sacrifice bunt, and Chase Meggers brought him home on a sacrifice fly for a 3-2 lead.

Mejias took the bottom of the 10th and delivered a perfect frame, striking out two before getting Matthew Miura to pop out to end it, earning his second save of the season.

The Mets improved to 7-13 in the second half and 40-46 overall. Palm Beach fell to 12-9 in the second half and 45-42 overall. St. Lucie can lock up the series Saturday night, with first pitch set for 6:30 p.m. at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium.

hero.headline: MLB restricts dugout iPad use to prevent artificial intelligence from making decisions
hero.teaser: Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make in-game decisions.
hero.body:
Major League Baseball made custom tabs on dugout iPads inaccessible to teams starting Wednesday night, when the second half of the season started, to prevent the tablets from running artificial intelligence to help make decisions. The tablets have access to video and league-provided data, and also included a custom tab where teams could access other programs. MLB executive vice president of baseball operations Morgan Sword wrote in a June 11 memo to general managers, assistant GMs and video coordinators that in many cases, the custom tab had expanded the use of the dugout iPads beyond their originally intended purpose to include recommendations regarding substitutions, pitch calling, and other in-game decisions traditionally made by players and coaches. The memo was first reported by The Athletic and obtained by The Associated Press.

A review by the competition committee found clubs had been compliant with the regulations. Sword wrote that instituting this prohibition beginning with the second half of the season is intended to provide clubs that have relied on the custom tab with appropriate lead-time to make any necessary adjustments. MLB started a pilot program allowing use of iPads in dugouts with restrictions late in the 2015 season and expanded their use in 2016 under a deal with Apple. Video was eliminated in the 2020 COVID season following the Houston Astros' sign-stealing scandal, then returned in 2021.

cards.headline: Britain's Josh Kerr breaks long-standing mile world record in London
cards.teaser: Josh Kerr ran the mile in 3:42.66 at Saturday's Diamond League event in London, breaking Hicham El Guerrouj's 27-year-old world record of 3:43.13 set in 1999.
cards.body:
Kerr made no secret that he was targeting the long-standing record at the Diamond League event in London. Earlier this week, he revealed he ran 2:42.45 in a 1,200-meter time trial. His sponsor, Brooks, dubbed the effort Project 222, referencing the number of seconds in 3 minutes, 42 seconds.

Kerr has emerged as one of the world's top middle-distance runners, winning bronze in the 1,500 meters at the Tokyo Olympics and silver at the 2024 Paris Olympics. Before turning professional, Kerr starred at the University of New Mexico, where he won multiple NCAA titles and set an NCAA indoor mile record of 3:35.01 in 2018. American Yared Nuguse finished second in Saturday's race in 3:45.69.

cards.headline: Security ramped up for World Cup final Sunday in New Jersey
cards.teaser: A sprawling network of federal agents, local law enforcement, and private companies continue with a game plan two years in the making to ensure Sunday's World Cup final between Argentina and Spain is safe.
cards.body:
A joint operations center in New York has helped oversee security and monitor threats in host cities throughout the tournament, with thousands of personnel on the ground and a team with an eye on the skies. The FBI has seized hundreds of drones flying in restricted airspace near stadiums during the tournament. For Sunday's match, FBI Special Agent Adam Kachhia-Patel says the agency will be getting live feeds and monitoring any drone activity in the area to see if there's anything they need to do from a threat perspective.

The final will include a beefed-up Secret Service perimeter, with President Trump attending the trophy presentation. White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt says his attendance will cap what has been the most watched, most secure, and most successful World Cup in American history. The World Cup final is a Level 1 Special Event, the highest possible security designation, with added resources from the Department of Homeland Security, the Department of Defense, and the FBI. No one will be allowed to simply walk up to the stadium or drive a personal vehicle. Those with a ticket must take approved transportation to the game and should arrive early to make their way through the stepped-up security.

cards.headline: Messi and Yamal's World Cup final matchup traces back to 2007 photo shoot
cards.teaser: Almost two decades ago, photographer Joan Monfort captured images of teenage Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub for a UNICEF charity calendar. Now they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press, took the photos in 2007 as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF. Luck dictated that Yamal's mother, who appears in the calendar photo, won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate. Soccer destiny then deemed that her baby boy, who would become a star for Barcelona some 15 years later, was paired up with the Argentine who would become the greatest of all time. A tearful Messi left Barcelona in 2021 when the club was in financial trouble. Yamal erupted at the club two years later.

Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship, when a teenage Yamal was enjoying his international breakout and led Spain to the title. The photo went viral then, but now, with the World Cup final looming, interest in his photos has skyrocketed. Monfort said he has been bombarded by queries for the photos by professional media outlets, while also seeing his images reproduced countless times on social media and the internet without any credit or compensation. The 19-year-old Yamal will face a Messi who is 20 years his senior in Sunday's final in New Jersey.

cards.headline: Argentina rallies past England with late goals to advance to World Cup final
cards.teaser: Argentina scored two goals in the final minutes to defeat England 2-1 in the World Cup semifinals Wednesday, with Lionel Messi assisting on both late strikes.
cards.body:
Argentina trailed 1-0 going into the 85th minute before rallying for a 2-1 victory over England on Wednesday to move one step closer to back-to-back World Cup titles. Enzo Fernandez scored the equalizer in the 85th minute after Lionel Messi fed him the ball, and Fernandez swept in a shot from outside the box. Substitute Lautaro Martinez then headed in the winner two minutes into stoppage time from a Messi cross. The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Martinez said he had predicted his match-winning contribution. "I dreamed it, I swear. I told Alexis (Mac Allister) that I was going to score. I told him that I was going to come on and I was going to win it," Martinez said. "I can tell you this team keeps showing what it's made of."

England took the lead when Anthony Gordon scored in the 55th minute but could not hold on. England goalkeeper Jordon Pickford made vital saves while Mac Allister sent a header off the post as wave after wave of Argentina attacks came. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. The loss marks the third time England has fallen in the World Cup semifinals after defeats to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. "I'm gutted for the team, the staff, the fans," England captain Harry Kane said. "We worked so hard to be here. The lads have given every bit of blood, sweat and tears. To fall short like we did is just gutting."

hero.headline: Declassified records show Chinese actor downloaded Florida voter data in 2022
hero.body:
President Donald Trump's national address on Thursday renewed debate over election security as newly released intelligence records revealed a Chinese cyber actor downloaded publicly available Florida voter-registration information from commercial websites in 2022. The declassified report also showed the same actor obtained records from Colorado, Connecticut, Michigan, Oklahoma and Rhode Island.

Another intelligence record lists Florida among 18 states whose voter information was obtained for possible identity matching and public-opinion analysis. The records describe the collection of voter information, some of it publicly available, but do not say Florida ballots or vote totals were altered. The 2022 report also says the actor's motive was unknown. The White House characterized the broader collection effort as a major compromise of American voter data. However, an earlier federal assessment of the 2022 elections found no evidence that detected foreign cyber activity prevented voting, changed votes or compromised the integrity of ballots.

The disclosure came as Trump urged Congress during his Thursday address to adopt tighter voting restrictions and repeated claims about the 2020 election that have not been substantiated. Trump did not single out Florida in his remarks, but the declassified records released by his White House did. The distinction between data collection and ballot manipulation remained important, as the records made clear that publicly available information was accessed rather than election systems being breached.

The week also brought major courtroom developments for two Florida lawmakers. Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map. U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Republican state Rep. Fabian Basabe ended the week facing a $450,000 civil judgment after a Leon County jury found him liable for sexual harassment, battery and defamation in a case brought by former legislative aide Nicolas Frevola, former intern Jacob Cutbirth and Frevola's mother. Basabe represented himself despite having no legal training, and the trial was repeatedly interrupted by procedural mistakes and violations of the judge's orders.

cards.headline: Rep. Angie Nixon gets September trial date for Capitol sit-in charges
cards.teaser: The Democratic state representative will stand trial on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May protest outside the governor's office over Florida's congressional map.
cards.body:
Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon learned she will stand trial the week of Sept. 21 on misdemeanor charges stemming from her May sit-in outside Gov. Ron DeSantis' Capitol office. Nixon and other protesters occupied the area for several hours while objecting to Florida's newly approved congressional map, which could help Republicans add up to four seats in the U.S. Capitol Police arrested Nixon after she refused an order to leave. Nixon calls the prosecution political and has incorporated the case into her campaign for U.S. Senate. She said following Wednesday's hearing that if they think the threat of a trial is going to make her back down, they picked the wrong woman.

The trial is scheduled after Florida's Aug. 18 primary, in which Nixon is challenging retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman for the Democratic Senate nomination. Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: South Florida residents change diets as E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks spread
cards.teaser: Thousands across the country have been affected by contaminated produce, including lettuce linked to Taco Bell locations, with confirmed cases in Palm Beach, St. Lucie and Martin counties.
cards.body:
Reports of contaminated produce continue to spread across the country, and many people in South Florida are changing what they eat and what they avoid. The latest concern centers around lettuce linked to outbreaks of E. coli and cyclospora, including lettuce connected to Taco Bell locations. Health officials said thousands across the U.S. have been affected, with confirmed cases also reported locally from the Palm Beaches into the Treasure Coast. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May: two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

At restaurants, grocery stores and fast-food chains, some families say they are steering clear of leafy greens altogether. In Boynton Beach, Hendriette Peckens said she bought two big bags of oranges, bread and some apples, and planned to cook Alaskan salmon for dinner. In downtown West Palm Beach, George Lorenz said he's taking precautions while grabbing lunch with his father, Brian, on Clematis Street. Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers. She recommends sticking to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel, but consumers still want to wash them before cutting into them and peeling them. Barone also recommends avoiding bagged lettuce if possible and instead buying whole heads of lettuce and peeling away the outer layers.

cards.headline: Alex Vindman raises $8.5 million in Florida U.S. Senate race
cards.teaser: The retired Army lieutenant's second-quarter fundraising brings his total receipts above $16 million as he faces Democratic Rep. Angie Nixon in the August primary.
cards.body:
Retired Army Lt. Alex Vindman tightened his grip on the Democratic money lead during the second quarter, raising $8.5 million and pushing his total receipts above $16 million. Vindman said he thinks it's safe to say that Republicans woke up this morning with a bit of a panic, and there's no denying that the Florida Senate race is in play. Vindman is challenging Democratic state Rep. Angie Nixon for the Democratic nomination in Florida's Aug. 18 primary.

Republican Sen. Ashley Moody reported raising another $3.6 million. Her campaign also promoted polling showing her leading either Vindman or Nixon in a potential general-election matchup. Moody was appointed to the Senate after Marco Rubio resigned to become secretary of state. The November special election will determine who serves the final two years of Rubio's term.

cards.headline: Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback faces court fight over residency
cards.teaser: Lt. Jay Collins argues records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor.
cards.body:
Next week will bring another political court fight as Republican gubernatorial candidate James Fishback defends his eligibility to remain in the primary. Lt. Jay Collins, one of Fishback's opponents, argues that records showing Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., mean he does not satisfy Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governor. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida and maintained the state as his permanent home.

A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin Tuesday in Tallahassee. Because primary ballots have already been printed, the judge has said a ruling against Fishback could require election officials to post notices and decline to count votes cast for him.

cards.headline: Dietitian recommends vinegar wash for produce during Florida contamination outbreaks
cards.teaser: Delray Medical Center expert says consumers should avoid bagged lettuce and use a 1-to-3 mixture of distilled white vinegar and water to clean fruits and vegetables.
cards.body:
Samantha Barone, dietitian for the bariatric program at Delray Medical Center, said consumers should focus on produce with protective outer layers amid the E. coli and cyclospora outbreaks. She told WPTV to stick to melon and things that have a harder skin that you can peel, but said the trick is you still want to wash them before you cut into them and peel them. That includes foods like bananas, melons and avocados. She also recommends washing all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating them and says beans and nuts are safe alternatives that still provide fiber and protein.

Barone's biggest warning is to avoid bagged lettuce if possible. Instead, she recommends buying whole heads of lettuce, peeling away the outer layers and avoiding berries, especially raspberries, because they are difficult to clean properly. She recommends cleaning produce using a 1-to-3 part mixture of distilled white vinegar and water, then soak, massage and clean off your produce and make sure to cook your vegetables. She said it's not an excuse to say to heck with fruits and vegetables and hit the donuts, emphasizing that people want to still remain healthy. According to the Florida Department of Health, there have been five confirmed local cases of cyclospora since May, with two in Palm Beach County, two in St. Lucie County and one in Martin County.

hero.headline: Martin County faces $2.1 billion transportation funding gap as needs outpace available money
hero.teaser: Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall, and the gap between what the county needs and what it can afford could shape how residents get around for decades.
hero.body:
Martin County is facing a $2.1 billion transportation funding shortfall over the next 20 years, a gap that could determine how residents travel for decades to come.

The Martin County Metropolitan Planning Organization estimates the county will need approximately $2.8 billion for transportation improvements through 2050, but only $701 million is currently available. That means the county can fund just about one quarter of its identified needs. Nearly all of the available funding comes from state and federal sources, with only $10 million coming from local revenue. The cost analysis was emailed to county and Stuart officials last August and outlines transportation needs across roads, transit, aviation, freight, and other infrastructure categories.

Among the most pressing unfunded needs are nine roads the county identified as requiring widening as traffic grows. The total cost to widen those roads is approximately $213 million, money that is not currently available, leaving all nine projects out of the county's draft Cost Feasible Plan. Those roads include SW Martin Downs Boulevard, SR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW 96th Street, SW Bridge Road, CR-714/SW Martin Highway, SW Allapattah Road/CR-609, SE Green River Parkway, SW Indiantown Avenue, and SE Bridge Road/CR-708. Without funding for these widening projects, the county will be unable to address growing congestion on these corridors.

State Road 710 stands out as among the county's highest priorities and has been the subject of repeated safety concerns. About $300 million in projects are planned for the corridor, reflecting the urgent need for improvements on this route. The massive funding shortfall highlights the challenge facing Martin County as it tries to balance transportation demands with limited financial resources over the coming decades.

hero.headline: Fort Pierce woman wins $5 million on Florida Lottery scratch-off ticket
hero.body:
Maria Duran, 57, of St. Lucie County claimed a $5 million top prize from the $5,000,000 CROSSWORD CASH scratch-off game on April 6, Florida Lottery officials announced Friday. Duran chose to receive her winnings as a one-time, lump-sum payment of $3,262,138.

Duran purchased her winning ticket from PK 2 Quick Mart, located at 4101 Okeechobee Road in Fort Pierce. The $20 scratch-off ticket turned into the multimillion-dollar jackpot.

The game's overall odds of winning are 1-in-2.90. The chance of winning the $5 million top prize playing this game is 1-in-4,018,135.

Florida Lottery officials released details of Duran's win on Friday, more than three months after she claimed the prize in April.

hero.headline: Waterspout crosses Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian as severe storms batter Treasure Coast
hero.body:
A large waterspout passed over the Indian River Lagoon near Sebastian Friday afternoon as severe weather left a trail of damage across the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County. Multiple videos sent to the WPTV newsroom captured the waterspout moving through the area during Friday's storm system.

The severe weather stretched across the region, bringing heavy rain, dangerous lightning and fires. In Port St. Lucie, weather spotter Merry Moore O'Rourke recorded over 3 inches of rain in her rain gauge. She described the sudden intensity of the storm, saying the sky got black, wind started raging and the sky lit up like she had not seen before. The severe weather extended to Okeechobee County, where fire rescue crews airlifted a man to the hospital after he was struck by lightning.

Lightning strikes ignited a brush fire near the 1900 block of Castinet Lane in Port St. Lucie after vegetation in a nearby lot caught fire. Lucie County Fire District crews contained that blaze. Fire crews also responded to a house fire at the 900 block of Bellevue Avenue during the evening storm. Radar picked up significant lightning activity in the area at the time, though Lucie County Fire District said it cannot confirm the cause as the fire marshal's office still needs to investigate.

Moore O'Rourke summed up the experience many residents felt as the storms moved through the region. "I mean it was radical. I mean it was a little scary," Moore O'Rourke said. Friday's severe weather served as a reminder of nature's unpredictable power, from waterspouts to lightning strikes and fires across the affected areas.
